cards.title: Introduction to Authentication
cards.content:
Authentication is the process of verifying who a user is, while authorization determines what they can do.

In Flask applications, we often use extensions like Flask-Login to manage user sessions securely.

cards.title: Securing Passwords
cards.content:
Never store plain text passwords in your database! Always hash them using a secure library like Werkzeug's security module.

from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash, check_password_hash

hashed_password = generate_password_hash('secret123')

options.text: Store passwords as plain text for easy retrieval.
Encrypt passwords with a reversible two-way cipher.
Hash passwords using a secure one-way hashing function like Werkzeug.

cards.title: Setting up Flask-Login
cards.content: Flask-Login handles user session management for Flask. To use it, your User model must implement specific properties and methods such as is_authenticated, is_active, is_anonymous, and get_id().

cards.title: Complete the Login Route
cards.content: To log a user in within a Flask route after verifying their credentials, we use the ___ function from Flask-Login.

steps: User submits username and password via a form.
Flask retrieves the user record from the database.
The submitted password is checked against the stored hash using check_password_hash.
Flask-Login creates a user session using login_user().

cards.title: Protecting Routes
cards.content:
You can restrict access to certain views for logged-in users only by using the @login_required decorator provided by Flask-Login.

@app.route('/dashboard')
@login_required
def dashboard():
    return 'Welcome to your dashboard!'
